text: The authors explain that Burns et al. (2024) normalize weak-to-strong gains by an 'upper-bound' from training the strong student on ground-truth labels (PGR). They argue that leveraging the weak supervisor's complementary knowledge might allow the weak-to-strong student to exceed that bound, questioning it, and so report raw accuracy gain instead.
title: Goel et al. question the 'upper-bound' in Burns et al.'s PGR metric for weak-to-strong
